text:
For a spin–½ particle the momentum–like operator  
  ⃗P = (ħ/2) ⃗σ ,  ⃗σ = (σx , σy , σz)  

acts on the two–component spinor.  
For a direction ⃗n lying in the x–z plane we can write  

  ⃗n = (sin θ, 0, cos θ) ,

so that the component of ⃗P along ⃗n is  

  Pn = (ħ/2)(⃗σ·⃗n) = (ħ/2)(sin θ σx + cos θ σz).

Using the Pauli matrices  

  σx = ⎛0  1⎞  σz = ⎛ 1  0⎞  
     ⎝1  0⎠     ⎝ 0 –1⎠ ,

the matrix for (2/ħ)Pn becomes  

  M = sin θ σx + cos θ σz  
    = ⎛ cos θ  sin θ ⎞  
    ⎝ sin θ –cos θ ⎠ .

The eigenvector |χ⟩ for the eigenvalue +1 of M (which corresponds to +ħ/2 of Pn) satisfies  

  M |χ⟩ = |χ⟩.

Let |χ⟩ = (a, b)ᵀ. Then  

1) cos θ a + sin θ b = a  
2) sin θ a – cos θ b = b.

From (1): (cos θ – 1)a + sin θ b = 0 ⇒ b/a = (1 – cos θ)/sin θ  
Using trigonometric identities,  

  1 – cos θ = 2 sin²(θ/2), sin θ = 2 sin(θ/2) cos(θ/2),

so b/a = tan(θ/2).

Choosing a normalization with a = cos(θ/2), we get b = sin(θ/2), and

  |χ⟩ = (cos (θ/2), sin (θ/2))ᵀ,

which is already normalized.

This matches option (B).

Answer: B
